megaraptor:eswiki:4.title: Megaraptor namunhuaiquii (Las garras de la mano)

facts.statement: The animal belongs to the genus Megaraptor.
facts.quote: genus: Megaraptor

facts.statement: The only named species is Megaraptor namunhuaiquii.
facts.quote: species: namunhuaiquii

facts.statement: Megaraptor lived during the Late Cretaceous, specifically from the Turonian to the Coniacian stages.
facts.quote: fossil_range: Late Cretaceous (Turonian – Coniacian)

facts.statement: The genus was described by Fernando E. Novas in 1998.
facts.quote: parent_authority: Novas, 1998

facts.statement: Fossils of Megaraptor have been found in the Portezuelo Formation in Patagonia, Argentina.
facts.quote: Its fossils have been discovered in the Patagonian Portezuelo Formation of Argentina, South America

facts.statement: The fossils date to roughly 90 to 88 million years ago.
facts.quote: dating to the Turonian and Coniacian ages of the Late Cretaceous, roughly 90–88 million years ago

facts.statement: The type specimen, consisting of fragmentary limb bones, was discovered in 1996 by Fernando E. Novas.
facts.quote: The type specimen of Megaraptor consists of a fragmentary assemblage of limb bones, discovered in 1996 by Argentine palaeontologist Fernando E. Novas

facts.statement: Megaraptor is estimated to have been about 8 meters long and weighed around 1 tonne.
facts.quote: It has been estimated that Megaraptor measured 8 m in length, and weighed around 1 tonnes

facts.statement: The skull was long, low, and slender, based primarily on a juvenile specimen.
facts.quote: Its skull, the anatomy of which is known primarily from a juvenile specimen, was long, low, and slender

facts.statement: The first finger claw measured 35 cm in total length, while the third finger claw was only 6.5 cm long.
facts.quote: the claw of the first finger measuring 35 cm in total length; the claw of the third finger was the smallest, only 6.5 cm in length

facts.statement: The environment was a fluvial deposit with a humid climate.
facts.quote: The depositional environment of the Portezuelo Formation was a fluvial (river) deposit, with a humid climate

facts.statement: While it was initially suggested to use claws to open carcasses, active predation is now generally favored.
facts.quote: It was initially suggested that Megaraptor may have used its hand claws to open carcasses, though a role in active predation is now generally favoured

facts.statement: It may have used large hand claws to grab prey and pull them toward its chest to be dispatched by its jaws.
facts.quote: Megaraptor, along with other megaraptorans such as Australovenator, may have relied on its large hand claws to grab prey items, pulling them towards its chest so that they could be dispatched by its jaws

facts.statement: Remains were recovered in January 1996 by Fernando E. Novas.
facts.quote: In January 1996, Argentine palaeontologist Fernando E. Novas recovered the fragmentary remains of a large theropod

facts.statement: The specimen was found in the Portezuelo Formation in Neuquén, northwestern Patagonia.
facts.quote: The specimen was discovered in strata belonging to the Portezuelo Formation, part of the Río Neuquén Subgroup in Neuquén, northwestern Patagonia

facts.statement: The specimen, catalogued as MCF-PVPH 79, was transported to the Museo Carmen Funes.
facts.quote: The specimen, catalogued as MCF-PVPH 79, was transported to the Museo Carmen Funes

facts.statement: Novas named the species Megaraptor namunhuaiquii.
facts.quote: Novas gave it the binomial name Megaraptor namunhuaiquii

facts.statement: The genus name comes from Greek 'mega' and Latin 'raptor', while the species name comes from Mapuche 'namun' and 'huaiqui'.
facts.quote: The genus name derives from the Greek mega (large) and the Latin raptor (thief), while the species name derives from the Mapuche namun (foot) and huaiqui (lance)

facts.statement: A second specimen, MUCPv 341, was described in 2004 by Jorge O. Calvo.
facts.quote: In 2004, a second Megaraptor specimen (MUCPv 341), was described in a paper helmed by Jorge O. Calvo

facts.statement: This specimen showed that the large claw belonged to the first finger, not the second toe.
facts.quote: it demonstrated that the large ungual belonged to the first digit of the manus, as opposed to the second digit of the foot

facts.statement: A third specimen, MUCPv 595, a juvenile partial skeleton, was discovered in 2005.
facts.quote: In 2005, a third M. namunhuaiquii specimen (MUCPv 595), consisting of the partial skeleton of a juvenile with uncertain affinities, was discovered

facts.statement: This third specimen was described in 2014 by Juan D. Porfiri.
facts.quote: It was described in 2014 by a team led by Juan D. Porfiri

facts.statement: The assignment of the juvenile specimen to M. namunhuaiquii has been questioned, even by its original describer.
facts.quote: The assignment of this specimen to M. namunhuaiquii has since been called into question, including by Porfiri himself

facts.statement: A 2025 paper noted morphological inconsistencies between the juvenile and larger specimens, questioning their referral to the same genus.
facts.quote: A paper published in 2025 by Maximilian Kellermann and colleagues noted morphological inconsistencies between the juvenile and other, larger specimens referred to M. namunhuaiquii

facts.statement: Researchers suggest the referral to a single genus may have been driven by the fact that specimens were found at the same locality.
facts.quote: Referral to a single genus, according to them, appeared to be driven largely by the fact that both specimens were found at the same locality

facts.statement: A fifth specimen, MUCPv 1353, was discovered in 2008.
facts.quote: A fifth specimen assigned to M. namunhuaiquii (MUCPv 1353) is known, discovered in 2008

facts.statement: This fifth specimen consists of skull material and much of the postcranial skeleton and has only been described in a thesis.
facts.quote: Consisting of assorted skull material and "a large part" of the postcranial skeleton, it has been described only in a thesis authored by Porfiri

facts.statement: Fernando Novas estimated the holotype to be around 8 meters long.
facts.quote: The holotype of Megaraptor was estimated by Fernando Novas to measure around 8 m in length

facts.statement: Gregory S. Paul estimated the length at 8 meters and weight at 1 tonne in 2010.
facts.quote: In 2010, Gregory S. Paul estimated its length at 8 m, its weight at 1 tonnes

facts.statement: Porfiri and colleagues estimated a mature specimen length of 9 to 10 meters in 2014 based on Allosaurus proportions.
facts.quote: Porfiri and colleagues, in their 2014 paper describing MUCPv 595, estimated the length of a mature specimen at 9–10 m based on the proportions of Allosaurus

facts.statement: Larramendi and Molina-Pérez estimated a body length of 8.3 meters, hip height of 2.35 meters, and mass of 1.3 tonnes in 2016.
facts.quote: In 2016, extrapolating instead from other megaraptorans, Asier Larramendi and Rubén Molina-Pérez estimated that M. namunhuaiquii had a body length of 8.3 m, a hip height of 2.35 m, and a body mass of 1.3 t

facts.statement: The Megaraptor skull was described as fairly gracile and weak compared to other theropods, likely due to the evolution of powerful forelimbs reducing the need for a strong skull in predation.
facts.quote: The skull was fairly gracile and weak compared to that of other theropods, possibly a consequence of the development of more powerful and mobile forelimbs and thus a decreased reliance on the skull for predation.

facts.statement: The premaxilla of Megaraptor is small and features several large foramina, a trait shared with many tyrannosauroids.
facts.quote: The premaxilla is fairly small and bears several large foramina, as in many tyrannosauroids.

facts.statement: The Megaraptor maxilla is long and subtriangular, displaying a mix of coelurosaur traits like a lengthened anterior ramus and allosauroid traits like a straight dorsal margin.
facts.quote: The maxilla is long and subtriangular, and has a combination of coelurosaur traits, such as the lengthening of the anterior (front) maxillary ramus, and allosauroid traits, such as the straightness of the dorsal (upper) margin.

facts.statement: The frontal bone of Megaraptor is quadrangular with a wide supratemporal fossa bounded by a strong ridge that meets the opposite side, resembling tyrannosauroids but differing from allosauroids.
facts.quote: The frontal is quadrangular, with a wide supratemporal fossa, bound by a strong ridge which contacted that of the opposite frontal, very similar to the condition seen in tyrannosauroids and unlike that of allosauroids.

facts.statement: At least four teeth were found in each premaxilla, and it is estimated that fifteen teeth were present in each maxilla of Megaraptor.
facts.quote: At least four teeth were present in each premaxilla, and presumably fifteen were present in each maxilla.

facts.statement: Megaraptor had heterodont teeth, with short, conical, D-shaped premaxillary teeth and larger, more recurved maxillary teeth.
facts.quote: The teeth were heterodont, meaning that two different tooth shapes were present: the premaxillary teeth were short and conical, almost D-shaped, whereas the maxillary teeth were larger and more recurved.

facts.statement: Each dentary of Megaraptor contained eighteen teeth, matching the count found in Australovenator.
facts.quote: Each dentary appears to have sported eighteen teeth, the same number as in Australovenator.

facts.statement: The neck of Megaraptor consisted of ten cervical vertebrae.
facts.quote: Megaraptor's neck contained ten cervical vertebrae.

facts.statement: All cervical vertebrae of Megaraptor were opisthocoelous, characterized by being convex at the front and concave at the back.
facts.quote: All of the cervical vertebrae were opisthocoelous, meaning that they were convex anteriorly and concave posteriorly (towards the back).

facts.statement: The sacrum of Megaraptor, a fused mass of vertebrae at the hips, consisted of five vertebrae.
facts.quote: The sacrum, a mass of fused vertebrae which sat at the hips, contained five vertebrae.

facts.statement: The forearm of Megaraptor measured 93.8 cm from the radius to the first digit, with the hand alone accounting for approximately 70 cm of that length.
facts.quote: M. namunhuaiquii's forearm, measured from the proximal (close to the body) end of the radius to the distal (far from the body) end of the first digit, measured 93.8 cm, with the manus alone comprising around 70 cm of that.

facts.statement: The first claw bone of Megaraptor was very large, measuring around 35 cm in length along its curve.
facts.quote: The first ungual (the bone supporting the claw) was very large, around 35 cm in length when measured along its curve.

facts.statement: The claw bones of Megaraptor were strongly curved, exhibiting more curvature than those found in spinosaurids.
facts.quote: Each of M. namunhuaiquii's unguals was strongly curved, more so than in spinosaurids.

facts.statement: In 2025, researchers used allometry to suggest that a fully mature Megaraptor skull would likely have been deeper, more robust, and had proportionally smaller eye sockets than the known juvenile specimen.
facts.quote: Allesio Ciaffi and colleagues, in 2025, used allometry to determine that the skull of a fully mature M. namunhuaiquii would likely have been deeper and more robust than that of MUCPv 595, and that the orbits (eye sockets) would have proportionally been smaller.

facts.statement: Researchers noted a caveat that the postcranial skeleton of Megaraptor contradicts allometric predictions, suggesting cranial allometry might also be unreliable.
facts.quote: They did, however, note the caveat that much of M. namunhuaiquii's postcranial skeleton (the elements posterior to the skull, or behind it) contradicts what might be assumed based on allometry alone, and that the same may apply to cranial elements.

facts.statement: Researchers initially suggested Megaraptor was a basal tetanuran rather than a coelurosaur.
facts.quote: In their reappraisal of the genus, Calvo and colleagues discounted the hypothesis that it was a coelurosaur, and suggested that it was instead a basal tetanuran, belonging to a clade that predated the split between allosauroids and coelurosaurs.

facts.statement: The clade Megaraptora was erected in 2012 to include Megaraptor namunhuaiquii and its closest relatives.
facts.quote: In 2012, Roger B. J. Benson, Matthew T. Carrano and Stephen L. Brusatte erected the clade Megaraptora to encompass M. namunhuaiquii and its closest relatives.

facts.statement: Megaraptorans were placed in the family Neovenatoridae and considered carcharodontosaurs in several studies.
facts.quote: Megaraptorans were placed within the family Neovenatoridae, and were therefore considered carcharodontosaurs, and the same result was recovered in several papers thereafter.

facts.statement: A 2014 analysis suggested megaraptorans were nested within Tyrannosauroidea.
facts.quote: The 2014 paper describing a juvenile M. namunhuaiquii suggested, based on a phylogenetic analysis, that megaraptorans were nested within Tyrannosauroidea.

facts.statement: The family Megaraptoridae was established to include Gondwanan megaraptorans closer to Megaraptor namunhuaiquii than to Fukuiraptor.
facts.quote: With the removal of Megaraptora from Neovenatoridae came the recognition of a new family, Megaraptoridae, consisting of Gondwanan taxa and defined as all megaraptorans closer to M. namunhuaiquii than to Fukuiraptor.

facts.statement: Recent analyses place Megaraptora within Coelurosauria as the sister taxon to Tyrannosauroidea.
facts.quote: Like some previous analyses by other authors, Megaraptora is nested within Coelurosauria, as the sister taxon to Tyrannosauroidea.

facts.statement: Megaraptor lived approximately 98 million years ago during the Late Cretaceous (Turonian to Coniacian) in what is now South America.
facts.quote: que vivió entre mediados a finales del período Cretácico, hace aproximadamente 98 millones de años, entre el Turoniense y el Coniaciense, en lo que hoy es Sudamérica.

facts.statement: The name Megaraptor namunhuaiquii means "giant thief with a spear in the foot" in Greek and Mapudungun.
facts.quote: El nombre Megaraptor namunhuaiquii proviene del griego y mapudungun, que significa "Ladrón gigante con lanza en el pie".

facts.statement: In 2007, researchers suggested Megaraptor used its forelimbs to open carcasses while using its head as the primary weapon.
facts.quote: Juan D. Porfiri, Domenica Dos Santos, and Jorge O. Calvo suggested in 2007 that Megaraptor may have used its forelimbs to open up carcasses, with the head serving as its primary weapon.

facts.statement: Researchers suggest Megaraptor likely had mobile forelimbs adapted to grip prey and draw them toward the jaws for dispatch.
facts.quote: The related Australovenator had very mobile forelimbs and wrists, possibly adapted to grip onto prey items and draw them towards the chest so that they could be dispatched via the jaws, and the same may have been true of megaraptorans overall, including M. namunhuaiquii itself.

facts.statement: It is debated whether Megaraptor was social or if found specimens represent natural post-mortem accumulation.
facts.quote: However, it was later suggested that the association of these specimens may be the result of deceased individuals naturally accumulating post-mortem.

facts.statement: Megaraptor had a small olfactory apparatus, suggesting olfaction played a limited role in its hunting.
facts.quote: The olfactory apparatus, the structures correlating to its sense of smell, were small compared to those of carcharodontosaurids and tyrannosaurids, indicating that the role of olfaction in hunting was limited.

facts.statement: Researchers noted that Megaraptor's actual hearing range was likely lower than calculations based on cochlear duct length suggest.
facts.quote: They did, however, acknowledge the limitations of using cochlear duct length to predict the acuity of hearing, and noted that the presence of tympanic sinuses (as in therizinosaurs) indicates that the actual hearing range was lower.

facts.statement: Megaraptor fossils are found in the Late Turonian to Early Coniacian Portezuelo Formation of Argentina.
facts.quote: Megaraptor is known from the Late Turonian to Early Coniacian-dated Portezuelo Formation of Argentina, part of the Río Neuquén Subgroup of the Neuquén Group.

facts.statement: Megaraptor lived in a humid environment with a meandering river system.
facts.quote: The depositional environment of the Portezuelo Formation was a meandering fluvial (river) system of varying sinuosity, with a humid climate.

facts.statement: The species name of the genus Megaraptor is M. namunhuaiquii.
facts.quote: name: Megaraptor namunhuaiquii

facts.statement: Megaraptor was a robust carnivorous theropod between 8 and 9 meters long.
facts.quote: Megaraptor fue un terópodo carnívoro de entre 8 y 9 metros de largo y de constitución robusta.

facts.statement: Its most notable feature was a sickle-shaped claw on the first finger measuring 42 centimeters in length.
facts.quote: La característica más notable era una garra en el dedo 1 de la mano en forma de hoz de 42 centímetros de largo.

facts.statement: Its hands were unusually long, bearing sickle-shaped claws that curved more than those of spinosaurids.
facts.quote: Las manos eran inusualmente alargadas, portando garras en forma de hoz que se curvaban aún más que las de los espinosáuridos.

facts.statement: It is debated whether Megaraptor is an allosaurid, carcarodontosaurid, megalosaurid, or something distinct from all known groups.
facts.quote: el hecho de si Megaraptor es o no un alosáurido, un carcarodontosáurido, un megalosáurido, o algo distinto a todo lo conocido es todavía motivo de diversas hipótesis.

facts.statement: Middle cervical vertebrae with a spherical anterior articular face and a cup-shaped posterior face, typical of tetanurans, are known from Megaraptor.
facts.quote: Se conocen de Megaraptor una serie de vértebras cervicales medias, con el centro cervical con una cara articular anterior esférica y una posterior en forma de copa para recibir a esta, típico de los tetanuros.

facts.statement: The neural spine lamina is short compared to Allosaurus, narrower at the base than the tip, with strong sites for the interspinous ligament on cranial and caudal faces.
facts.quote: La lámina de la espina neural es corta comparada con la de Allosaurus, siendo más angosta en la base que en el extremo y las caras craneal y caudal presentan fuertes sitios para el ligamento interespinoso.

facts.statement: Only two articulated proximal caudal vertebrae, slightly compressed laterally, have been recovered.
facts.quote: Solo dos vértebras caudales articuladas de la porción proximal de la cola se han recuperado, ligeramente comprimidas en lateral.

facts.statement: The scapula extends cranio-caudally in a long, narrow sword shape, with a concave cranial edge and a slightly convex caudal edge.
facts.quote: La escápula se extiende craneocaudalmente en forma de espada, larga y angosta, el borde craneal es cóncavo y el caudal ligeramente convexo.

facts.statement: The known forelimb elements (ulna, radius, and hand) measure 93.8 centimeters in length, with the hand alone measuring 70 centimeters.
facts.quote: Del miembro anterior se conoce la ulna, el radio y la mano, que miden 93,8 centímetros de largo, la mano sola mide 70 centímetros.

facts.statement: The ulna is a dense bone with a prominent, transversely compressed olecranon resembling that of Baryonyx.
facts.quote: La ulna es un hueso denso con un prominente y transversalmente comprimido olécranon que hace recordar al de Baryonyx.

facts.statement: The pubis of Megaraptor has a completely open obturator foramen, unlike in more basal theropods.
facts.quote: El pubis del Megaraptor tiene un foramen obturador completamente abierto, a diferencia de los terópodos más basales.

facts.statement: The hand is Megaraptor's most outstanding feature, especially fingers I and II which possess very developed ungual phalanges.
facts.quote: La mano de Megaraptor es su característica más sobresaliente, en especial los dedos I y II que poseen falanges ungulares muy desarrolladas.

facts.statement: Fingers I, II, and III are well-developed with phalanx formulas of 2, 3, and 4, while finger IV is rudimentary and lacks phalanges.
facts.quote: Los dedos I, II y III están bien desarrollados con una fórmulas de falanges 2, 3 y 4, pero el dedo IV es rudimentario y le faltan falanges.

facts.statement: This claw exhibits a groove uniting both sides on the outer curve near the base, very similar to that found on the second finger claw of deinonychosaurs.
facts.quote: Esta garra exhibe un surco que une a ambos sobre la curva externa, cerca de la base, muy similar a la encontrada en la garra del segundo dedo de los deinicosaurios.

facts.statement: Despite having a poorly developed flexor tubercle and lacking a tendon fossa in that tubercle, this claw measured around 35 centimeters in a straight line from tip to base.
facts.quote: Aunque presenta dos grandes diferencias, un tubérculo flexor muy poco desarrollado y le falta la fosa para el tendón en este mismo tubérculo, esta garra medía alrededor de 35 centímetros, en línea recta desde la punta a la base.

facts.statement: Finger II possessed three robust phalanges with an ungual phalanx of around 24 centimeters, symmetrical on both faces, with two grooves at the same level as in Fukuiraptor.
facts.quote: El dedo II poseía tres robustas falanges con una falange ungular de alrededor de 24 centímetros, siendo simétrica en ambas caras, con dos surcos ubicados en el mismo nivel que el Fukuiraptor.

facts.statement: Metacarpal I is short and massive, with the distal half deviated medially, and distal condyles separated by a groove.
facts.quote: El metacarpo I es corto, masivo y la mitad distal desviada hacia medial, los cóndilos distales están separados por un surco.

facts.statement: Megaraptor was described in 1998 by Fernando Novas, initially as a large carnivore probably belonging to the dromaeosaurid family.
facts.quote: Megaraptor fue descripto en 1998 por Fernando Novas, inicialmente como un carnívoro de gran tamaño, probablemente perteneciente a la familia de los dromeosáuridos.

facts.statement: The remains come from the Portezuelo Formation of the Neuquén Group, on the north coast of Lake Barreales in Neuquén Province, Argentina.
facts.quote: Los restos provienen de la Formación Portezuelo, del el Grupo Neuquén, sobre la costa norte del Lago Barreales, en la Provincia del Neuquén, Argentina.

facts.statement: The second specimen, MUCPv-341, includes an anterior cervical vertebra, scapula, coracoid, ulna, radius, a complete hand, pubis, two caudal vertebrae with hemal arches, and metatarsal IV.
facts.quote: El segundo espécimen, MUCPv-341, incluye una vértebra cervical anterior, escápula, coracoides, ulna, radio, una mano completa, pubis, dos vértebras caudales con arco hemal y metatarso IV.

facts.statement: Megaraptor lived during the Turonian to Coniacian stages, from 93.9 to 85.7 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Turonian to Coniacian (93.9 to 85.7 million years ago)

facts.statement: The parent group of Megaraptor is Megaraptoridae.
facts.quote: Parent group: Megaraptoridae

facts.statement: Megaraptor belongs to the family Megaraptoridae.
facts.quote: Family: Megaraptoridae

facts.statement: Megaraptor is classified in the class Reptilia.
facts.quote: Class: Reptilia
